title: Sovereign immunity and statutory tort waivers
shortTitle: Sovereign immunity and statutory tort waivers
summary: Sovereign immunity protects the government from suit unless an applicable legal waiver permits the claim.
notes:
The Federal Tort Claims Act supplies a broad waiver for specified employee torts under conditions tied to private liability under local law, while section 2680 preserves exceptions. In Raila and Dolan, the question was the scope of one exception rather than whether every alleged injury automatically created liability. A claimant who clears the immunity issue still must establish the remaining requirements of a valid claim.

The Third Circuit relied on a presumption favoring the sovereign. The Supreme Court found that approach unhelpful when an expansive reading of an exception would defeat the broad waiver. This is a contextual treatment of the Federal Tort Claims Act; it should not be generalized into abandonment of every sovereign-immunity clear-statement principle.
